Guthild:

I can’t remember a time when we had good customer service for this game.

The BC era was when Blizzard customer service was second to none. There were multiple avenues to contact support. Email, forums, telephone (!), in-game Gamemasters who were enthusiastic to say the least, and devs actually hung out in the forums and explained stuff.

Then Cataclysm happened in more ways than one. For the first time an expansion had serious problems at launch, and customer service started retreating on all fronts. By the end of Mists the last devs had left the General forums, the phone lines were gone, and if there were any in-game GMs, they were pretty much in hiding.

The Customer Support forum is about the last place to connect with a human for help.

posts.name: Gobstopper
posts.cooked:
I’ve noticed something interesting: A lot of people seem to think support are against them. Like they’re just trying their hardest to leave someone frustrated and not be able to help them.

I’m not sure where this attitude came from, but I’m 99% positive this isn’t the case?

Anyway: There’s no AI used in Support. You get a response from a person. Sometimes you get a response in a template, which is typical in a service space, but AI responses are not used.

You can believe it or not, that is from the Customer Service forums from Customer Service reps, who I imagine have a better idea how things work over there than most.

I can say that most of my support experiences have been pleasant. There were some TRP3 (an RP addon) experiences where the GM didn’t understand it was an addon and gave incorrect directions, but I have learned to make the ticket more detailed to prevent it from happening twice. I never had the problem again.

I understand some have had ongoing issues, but a good portion of those are things that GMs can’t flat out help with, or under incorrect categories and going to the wrong people. You can look at the Customer Service forums and see people who have been able to be helped on a pretty regular basis. Some things make helping much more difficult, like providing false information in an account which makes verification impossible, but that’s not really support’s fault, is it?

Support isn’t out to get anyone. They’re trying to help. Sometimes there’s some hurdles to be jumped if they can help at all.

Because they have shifted CS work from low to mid-level higher paid full time US based employees with reasonable levels of autonomy to lower than entry level lower paid part time and contract potentially even offshore employees following explicit scripts with no autonomy whatsoever, all the while reducing the overall number of CS agents.

Old CS were full time Blizzard employees with enough training and skill to be allowed to provide service by taking actions in-game (controlled and monitored, but they had some ability to use their judgement to assist players).

New CS (especially first level) are most likely not even Blizzard employees, and they are given the bare minimum of training to follow explicit scripts, and have no ability to think independently or take actions to solve customer issues.

If the developers have not taken ownership of an issue and given the new CS an explicit step by step script on how to handle, new CS is basically told to tell you to ‘check wowhead’ and / or ‘submit a bug report’.
